source.name: tr_OrderAudit
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE   TRIGGER dbo.tr_OrderAudit
ON dbo.Orders
AFTER INSERT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    INSERT INTO dbo.OrderMetadata (OrderID, MetadataXml)
    SELECT i.OrderID, CAST('<audit><timestamp>' + CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), GETDATE(), 126) + '</timestamp></audit>' AS XML)
    FROM inserted i
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.OrderMetadata m WHERE m.OrderID = i.OrderID);
END;

result.generatedDdl:
-- Trigger function for OrderAudit
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.tr_OrderAudit_func()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Insert audit metadata for new orders that don't already have metadata
    INSERT INTO dbo.OrderMetadata (OrderID, MetadataXml)
    SELECT i.OrderID, 
           XMLPARSE(DOCUMENT '<audit><timestamp>' || TO_CHAR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '</timestamp></audit>')
    FROM new_table i
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM dbo.OrderMetadata m 
        WHERE m.OrderID = i.OrderID
    );
    
    RETURN NULL; -- AFTER trigger on statement level
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Trigger binding
CREATE TRIGGER tr_OrderAudit
AFTER INSERT ON dbo.Orders
REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS new_table
FOR EACH STATEMENT
EXECUTE FUNCTION dbo.tr_OrderAudit_func();
assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
The OrderMetadata table exists with columns OrderID and MetadataXml of type XML
The Orders table has an OrderID column
SET NOCOUNT ON is not needed in PostgreSQL (no equivalent required)
GETDATE() converted to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP for PostgreSQL
SQL Server's CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), GETDATE(), 126) format (ISO8601) mapped to TO_CHAR with 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS' format
CAST AS XML converted to XMLPARSE(DOCUMENT ...) for PostgreSQL XML type
Statement-level trigger used since the original trigger processes the inserted table as a set

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that the XML format and timestamp format match application requirements. SQL Server's style 126 includes fractional seconds; adjust TO_CHAR format if milliseconds are needed (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS')
Transition tables require PostgreSQL 10+. Verify PostgreSQL version compatibility
Verify that the NOT EXISTS logic handles concurrent inserts appropriately. Consider if a unique constraint on OrderMetadata.OrderID would be beneficial to prevent race conditions
reviewFlags.codeSection: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.OrderMetadata m WHERE m.OrderID = i.OrderID)

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's CONVERT style 126 produces ISO8601 format with fractional seconds (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:45.123). The PostgreSQL conversion uses TO_CHAR without milliseconds. Add '.MS' to the format string if fractional seconds are required.
PostgreSQL's XML type and XMLPARSE function may have stricter validation than SQL Server's XML CAST. Ensure the XML structure is well-formed and valid.

Both SQL Server and PostgreSQL execute this as a statement-level trigger (once per INSERT statement), so behavior should be consistent. However, PostgreSQL requires explicit REFERENCING clause for transition tables.
PostgreSQL triggers execute within the same transaction as the triggering statement. If the trigger fails, the entire operation rolls back, which matches SQL Server behavior.
